page.overview:
What is Galathil?

Galathil was the grandson of Thingol's younger brother Elmo. He was son of Galadhon and brother of Celeborn. Galathil was the father of Nimloth, who later wedded Dior and became the Queen of Doriath.

Galathil and his close kin shared names with the White Trees.

The conception of this name was based on Tolkien's idea that Celeborn's name was first devised to mean "Silver Tree", and his close kin all had "tree-names". Although he later changed what he wanted Celeborn's name to mean, referring to "silver" and "tall" from the adjective ornâ ("uprising, tall") instead of "silver" and "tree" from the noun ornê ("tree"), he did not revise the name meanings of his close kin.

Based on Tolkien's original version of the family's names, Galathil is a name that can be seen in the tree name Galathilion, which was another name for Telperion. This was also the name of the White Tree of Tirion, 'Galathilion the Less', and its seedlings were Celeborn in Tol Eressëa and Nimloth in Númenor.
